label: Actual-root favourings are good-general, from nonlimitation and the formal object
meaning: Fix an actual root r at w and a favouring determination favours phi of r. Actual roots have no represented limiting principle (its distinct simply prior being is the shared CausalityFrame's PriorSimply, PRIOR_1), so by the RootPurity bridge every real determination of r is pure, favours phi among them. By the per-bearer bridge, phi favours x over y exactly where its formal object ranks x over y, and by the object premise that object is the value order v's relation (STANDARD_OF_FAVOURING_1). Betterness varies within an end-realization class: some x is better than y at s, at least one of them not a present input, and not at a scenario t that agrees with s on end-realization. Then phi favours x over y at s and not at t, so phi depends on betterness with end-realization fixed (BECAUSE_OF_GOODNESS_2) and is good-general. The main theorem uses no axioms. Neither the per-bearer bridge nor the object premise mentions whether the favouring is a natural or a rational appetite, so the route is mode-neutral. It is a conditional alternative formulation inside the purity family that splits lane P's value-sense bridges (b86a2364) into a part the D-directed rival accepts (the per-bearer bridge) and the part it denies (the object premise); it adds no independent warrant to e2357adc's rationale. It does not use the #2153 admissible family, joint compossibility, the purity of good-generality e2357adc, one-favouring realization 3e6ae3e7, the E premise or the cognition criterion. Comparator companions (Mathlib axioms): formalObjectControls gives, on the #2153 two-being carrier with the Lane 2b profiles, a positive witness (also realized as a natural appetite with no apprehension, where the cognition criterion fails) and for each non-logical premise a row where it fails, the others hold and the conclusion fails; its fifth row is the D-directed nature measured by its own end, where only the object premise fails. appetiteGrid gives the four mode-by-object cells: the good-tracking profile as a natural appetite of a content state and as a rational appetite of a full apprehension state, both good-general; the D-directed profile as a natural appetite of a state determined to one end; the determined will as a rational appetite; per-bearer and common-value verdicts, which read only the profile and so are the same in both good-tracking cells; and the cognition criterion, which on the same good-tracking source holds when the source apprehends and fails when nothing is apprehended. The assignments say nothing about what favouring, purity, value, nature or apprehension are.
